import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.4

by M. R. Vaughan-Lee

Construct a finite centrally nilpotent loop whose laws have no finite basis.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.4»

/-- A loop, presented in its equational signature: an identity, multiplication,
and left and right division. -/
structure Loop (L : Type*) where
  one : L
  mul : L → L → L
  ldiv : L → L → L
  rdiv : L → L → L
  one_mul : ∀ x, mul one x = x
  mul_one : ∀ x, mul x one = x
  ldiv_mul : ∀ x y, ldiv x (mul x y) = y
  mul_ldiv : ∀ x y, mul x (ldiv x y) = y
  mul_rdiv : ∀ x y, mul (rdiv x y) y = x
  rdiv_mul : ∀ x y, rdiv (mul x y) y = x

/-- A congruence of a loop is an equivalence relation compatible with every
operation in the loop signature. -/
structure LoopCongruence {L : Type*} (A : Loop L) where
  rel : L → L → Prop
  refl : ∀ x, rel x x
  symm : ∀ {x y}, rel x y → rel y x
  trans : ∀ {x y z}, rel x y → rel y z → rel x z
  mul : ∀ {x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂}, rel x₁ x₂ → rel y₁ y₂ → rel (A.mul x₁ y₁) (A.mul x₂ y₂)
  ldiv : ∀ {x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂}, rel x₁ x₂ → rel y₁ y₂ → rel (A.ldiv x₁ y₁) (A.ldiv x₂ y₂)
  rdiv : ∀ {x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂}, rel x₁ x₂ → rel y₁ y₂ → rel (A.rdiv x₁ y₁) (A.rdiv x₂ y₂)

/-- An element is central modulo a congruence if its image in the quotient
commutes and associates, in each of the three positions, with all elements. -/
def IsCentralModulo {L : Type*} (A : Loop L) (c : LoopCongruence A) (x : L) : Prop :=
  (∀ y, c.rel (A.mul x y) (A.mul y x)) ∧
  (∀ y z, c.rel (A.mul (A.mul x y) z) (A.mul x (A.mul y z))) ∧
  (∀ y z, c.rel (A.mul (A.mul y x) z) (A.mul y (A.mul x z))) ∧
  (∀ y z, c.rel (A.mul (A.mul y z) x) (A.mul y (A.mul z x)))

/-- Bruck central nilpotency: there is a finite central congruence series from
equality to the universal congruence. -/
def IsCentrallyNilpotent {L : Type*} (A : Loop L) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin (n + 1) → LoopCongruence A),
    (∀ x y, (c 0).rel x y ↔ x = y) ∧
    (∀ x y, (c (Fin.last n)).rel x y) ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n,
      (∀ x y, (c i.castSucc).rel x y → (c i.succ).rel x y) ∧
      ∀ x, (c i.succ).rel x A.one → IsCentralModulo A (c i.castSucc) x

/-- Terms in the loop signature, with variables indexed by natural numbers. -/
inductive LoopTerm where
  | var : ℕ → LoopTerm
  | one : LoopTerm
  | mul : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | ldiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | rdiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- Simultaneous substitution of loop terms for variables. -/
def LoopTerm.subst (σ : ℕ → LoopTerm) : LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | .var i => σ i
  | .one => .one
  | .mul t u => .mul (t.subst σ) (u.subst σ)
  | .ldiv t u => .ldiv (t.subst σ) (u.subst σ)
  | .rdiv t u => .rdiv (t.subst σ) (u.subst σ)

/-- A law in the loop signature is an equation between two terms. -/
abbrev LoopLaw := LoopTerm × LoopTerm

/-- Evaluation of a loop term under an assignment of its variables. -/
def LoopTerm.eval {L : Type*} (A : Loop L) (v : ℕ → L) : LoopTerm → L
  | .var i => v i
  | .one => A.one
  | .mul t u => A.mul (t.eval A v) (u.eval A v)
  | .ldiv t u => A.ldiv (t.eval A v) (u.eval A v)
  | .rdiv t u => A.rdiv (t.eval A v) (u.eval A v)

/-- The assertion that a law holds for every assignment in a loop. -/
def Satisfies {L : Type*} (A : Loop L) (e : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → L, e.1.eval A v = e.2.eval A v

/-- Derivability from a set of laws by the standard rules of equational logic. -/
inductive Derives (S : Set LoopLaw) : LoopLaw → Prop where
  | assumption {e} : e ∈ S → Derives S e
  | refl (t) : Derives S (t, t)
  | symm {t u} : Derives S (t, u) → Derives S (u, t)
  | trans {t u w} : Derives S (t, u) → Derives S (u, w) → Derives S (t, w)
  | mul {t₁ t₂ u₁ u₂} : Derives S (t₁, t₂) → Derives S (u₁, u₂) →
      Derives S (.mul t₁ u₁, .mul t₂ u₂)
  | ldiv {t₁ t₂ u₁ u₂} : Derives S (t₁, t₂) → Derives S (u₁, u₂) →
      Derives S (.ldiv t₁ u₁, .ldiv t₂ u₂)
  | rdiv {t₁ t₂ u₁ u₂} : Derives S (t₁, t₂) → Derives S (u₁, u₂) →
      Derives S (.rdiv t₁ u₁, .rdiv t₂ u₂)
  | subst {t u} : Derives S (t, u) → (σ : ℕ → LoopTerm) →
      Derives S (t.subst σ, u.subst σ)

/-- A loop has no finite basis for its laws if no finite set of laws valid in
the loop derives every law valid in the loop. -/
def HasNoFiniteBasis {L : Type*} (A : Loop L) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ S : Set LoopLaw, S.Finite ∧
      (∀ e ∈ S, Satisfies A e) ∧
      ∀ e, Satisfies A e → Derives S e

/--
Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws. Here
nilpotent means centrally nilpotent in Bruck's sense: a finite upper central
series reaches the whole loop. Laws and their consequences are taken in the
signature consisting of the identity, multiplication, and left and right
division.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.4» :
    ∃ (L : Type) (A : Loop L), Finite L ∧ IsCentrallyNilpotent A ∧ HasNoFiniteBasis A := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.4»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.4

by M. R. Vaughan-Lee

Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws.

A loop is a set with a multiplication and an identity element in which the equations
$a x = b$ and $y a = b$ have unique solutions $x$ and $y$. Loops form a variety of algebras in
the signature $(\cdot, \backslash, /, 1)$ of multiplication, left division, right division and
identity, and the *laws* of a loop $L$ are the identities $s \approx t$ between terms of this
signature that hold in $L$. The laws of $L$ have a *finite basis* if some finite set of laws
of $L$ has every law of $L$ as a consequence. By the Oates–Powell theorem the laws of every
finite group have a finite basis; the problem asks for a finite nilpotent loop for which this
fails.

*Nilpotent* is Bruck's central nilpotency for loops: the centre $Z(L)$ of $L$ consists of the
elements that commute and associate with all elements of $L$, it is a normal subloop, and $L$ is
nilpotent if its upper central series $1 = Z_0 \le Z_1 \le \dots$, with
$Z_{i+1}/Z_i = Z(L/Z_i)$, reaches $L$ after finitely many steps. Equivalently, $L$ has a
finite central series, i.e. a chain of normal subloops $1 = N_0 \le N_1 \le \dots \le N_n = L$
with $N_{i+1}/N_i \le Z(L/N_i)$ for all $i < n$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.4»

/-- A loop: a type with a multiplication `*`, an identity element `1`, a left division `ldiv`
and a right division `/` such that `x * ldiv x y = y`, `ldiv x (x * y) = y`, `(y / x) * x = y`
and `(y * x) / x = y` for all `x y`. Equivalently, a type with a multiplication and an identity
element in which the equations `a * x = b` and `y * a = b` have unique solutions `x` and `y`,
namely `x = ldiv a b` and `y = b / a`. -/
class Loop (L : Type*) extends MulOneClass L, Div L where
  /-- Left division: `ldiv x y` is the unique solution `z` of `x * z = y`. -/
  ldiv : L → L → L
  mul_ldiv_cancel (x y : L) : x * ldiv x y = y
  ldiv_mul_cancel (x y : L) : ldiv x (x * y) = y
  div_mul_cancel (x y : L) : (y / x) * x = y
  mul_div_cancel (x y : L) : (y * x) / x = y

/-- Terms in the signature `(*, ldiv, /, 1)` of loops, over the countably infinite set of
variables `x₀, x₁, x₂, …` indexed by `ℕ`. -/
inductive LoopTerm : Type
  /-- The variable `xᵢ`. -/
  | var (i : ℕ)
  /-- The constant `1`. -/
  | one
  /-- The product `s * t`. -/
  | mul (s t : LoopTerm)
  /-- The left quotient `ldiv s t`. -/
  | ldiv (s t : LoopTerm)
  /-- The right quotient `s / t`. -/
  | div (s t : LoopTerm)

/-- The value of a term in a loop `L` under an assignment `v : ℕ → L` of the variables. -/
def LoopTerm.eval {L : Type*} [Loop L] (v : ℕ → L) : LoopTerm → L
  | var i => v i
  | one => 1
  | mul s t => s.eval v * t.eval v
  | ldiv s t => Loop.ldiv (s.eval v) (t.eval v)
  | div s t => s.eval v / t.eval v

/-- A law (identity) in the signature of loops: a pair of terms `(s, t)`, read as the
equation `s ≈ t`. -/
abbrev LoopLaw : Type := LoopTerm × LoopTerm

namespace Loop

variable (L : Type*) [Loop L]

/-- The law `e = (s, t)` holds in the loop `L` if `s` and `t` take the same value in `L` under
every assignment of the variables. -/
def Satisfies (e : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → L, e.1.eval v = e.2.eval v

/-- The set of all laws of the loop `L`. -/
def laws : Set LoopLaw :=
  {e | Satisfies L e}

/-- A set `S` of laws implies the law `e` if every loop satisfying all the laws in `S` also
satisfies `e`. By Birkhoff's completeness theorem this is the same as `e` being derivable from
`S` (together with the defining identities of loops) in equational logic. -/
def Implies (S : Set LoopLaw) (e : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : Type) [Loop M], (∀ e' ∈ S, Satisfies M e') → Satisfies M e

/-- The laws of the loop `L` have a finite basis if there is a finite set of laws of `L` which
implies every law of `L`. -/
def HasFiniteBasis : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Finset LoopLaw, ↑S ⊆ laws L ∧ ∀ e ∈ laws L, Implies S e

variable {L}

/-- A congruence on the loop `L`: an equivalence relation on `L` compatible with `*`, `ldiv`
and `/`. Congruences on `L` correspond bijectively to normal subloops of `L`, a congruence `r`
corresponding to the normal subloop `{m | r 1 m}`. -/
structure IsCongruence (r : L → L → Prop) : Prop where
  equivalence : Equivalence r
  mul {a b c d : L} : r a b → r c d → r (a * c) (b * d)
  ldiv {a b c d : L} : r a b → r c d → r (ldiv a c) (ldiv b d)
  div {a b c d : L} : r a b → r c d → r (a / c) (b / d)

/-- The element `m` is central modulo the relation `r`: `m` commutes and associates with all
elements of `L` up to `r`. When `r` is equality this says that `m` lies in the centre $Z(L)$,
and when `r` is the congruence of a normal subloop `N` it says that the coset `m N` lies in the
centre of `L / N`. -/
def IsCentralMod (r : L → L → Prop) (m : L) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : L, r (m * x) (x * m) ∧ r (m * (x * y)) ((m * x) * y) ∧
    r (x * (m * y)) ((x * m) * y) ∧ r (x * (y * m)) ((x * y) * m)

variable (L)

/-- The loop `L` is (centrally) nilpotent, in the sense of Bruck, if it has a finite central
series. Normal subloops are described by their congruences: a central series of length `n` is
a chain of congruences `θ 0 ≤ θ 1 ≤ … ≤ θ n` on `L`, with `θ 0` the equality relation and
`θ n` the total relation, such that for every `i < n` every element `m` that is
`θ (i + 1)`-congruent to `1` is central modulo `θ i`. In terms of the normal subloops
`N i = {m | θ i 1 m}` this is a chain `1 = N 0 ≤ N 1 ≤ … ≤ N n = L` with
`N (i + 1) / N i ≤ Z(L / N i)` for all `i < n`. Equivalently, the upper central series of `L`
reaches `L` after finitely many steps. -/
def IsNilpotent : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (θ : ℕ → L → L → Prop),
    (∀ i, IsCongruence (θ i)) ∧
    (∀ a b, θ 0 a b ↔ a = b) ∧
    (∀ a b, θ n a b) ∧
    (∀ i < n, ∀ a b, θ i a b → θ (i + 1) a b) ∧
    (∀ i < n, ∀ m, θ (i + 1) 1 m → IsCentralMod (θ i) m)

end Loop

/--
Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws.

That is: there is a finite, centrally nilpotent loop `L` whose laws (the identities in the
signature `(*, ldiv, /, 1)` of loops that hold in `L`) have no finite basis, i.e. no finite
set of laws of `L` has every law of `L` as a consequence. This is the loop-theoretic
counterpart of the Oates–Powell theorem, which says that the laws of every finite group have a
finite basis.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.4» :
    ∃ (L : Type) (_ : Loop L), Finite L ∧ Loop.IsNilpotent L ∧ ¬ Loop.HasFiniteBasis L := by
  sorry

/-- Every group is a loop, with left division `ldiv a b = a⁻¹ * b` and the usual right
division `a / b = a * b⁻¹`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
def Loop.ofGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Loop G where
  ldiv a b := a⁻¹ * b
  mul_ldiv_cancel := mul_inv_cancel_left
  ldiv_mul_cancel := inv_mul_cancel_left
  div_mul_cancel x y := _root_.div_mul_cancel y x
  mul_div_cancel x y := _root_.mul_div_cancel_right y x

/-- The law `x₀ * 1 ≈ x₀` holds in every loop. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem Loop.satisfies_mul_one (L : Type*) [Loop L] :
    Loop.Satisfies L (.mul (.var 0) .one, .var 0) :=
  fun _ => mul_one _

/-- An abelian group is a nilpotent loop (with a central series of length one). -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem Loop.ofGroup_isNilpotent (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] :
    letI := Loop.ofGroup G
    Loop.IsNilpotent G := by
  letI := Loop.ofGroup G
  refine ⟨1, fun i a b => i = 0 → a = b, fun i => ?_, fun a b => ⟨fun h => h rfl, fun h _ => h⟩,
    fun a b h => absurd h one_ne_zero, fun i _ a b _ h => absurd h i.succ_ne_zero,
    fun i hi m _ x y => ?_⟩
  · exact
      { equivalence :=
          ⟨fun _ _ => rfl, fun h hi => (h hi).symm, fun h h' hi => (h hi).trans (h' hi)⟩
        mul := fun h h' hi => by rw [h hi, h' hi]
        ldiv := fun h h' hi => by rw [h hi, h' hi]
        div := fun h h' hi => by rw [h hi, h' hi] }
  · obtain rfl : i = 0 := by omega
    exact ⟨fun _ => mul_comm m x, fun _ => (mul_assoc m x y).symm, fun _ => (mul_assoc x m y).symm,
      fun _ => (mul_assoc x y m).symm⟩

/-- The laws of the trivial loop have a finite basis, namely the single law `x₀ ≈ x₁`. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem Loop.hasFiniteBasis_unit :
    letI := Loop.ofGroup Unit
    Loop.HasFiniteBasis Unit := by
  letI := Loop.ofGroup Unit
  refine ⟨{(.var 0, .var 1)}, fun _ _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun e _ M _ hM => ?_⟩
  haveI : Subsingleton M :=
    ⟨fun a b => hM _ (Finset.mem_singleton_self _) (fun i => if i = 0 then a else b)⟩
  exact fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _

end Kourovka.«8.4»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single slot matches the one-sentence statement, and the notes' reading (existence; Bruck central nilpotency; laws in the loop signature; finite basis = finite set of laws with all laws as equational consequences) is the standard one and was followed.
modeling_decisions: Imperative 'Construct …' is formalized as a plain existence statement (no answer(sorry)), following the repository convention for imperative problems (cf. Wikipedia/SteinerSystem.lean) and the decomposition note.

Loops are taken in the equational signature (*, ldiv, /, 1) with the four division identities x*ldiv x y = y, ldiv x (x*y) = y, (y/x)*x = y, (y*x)/x = y (equivalent to unique solvability of a*x = b and y*a = b). Laws are pairs of terms in this signature over variables indexed by ℕ. For a finite loop the divisions are term-definable from multiplication, so finite basability does not depend on this signature choice.

Equational consequence `Loop.Implies S e` is semantic: every loop M : Type satisfying S satisfies e. By Birkhoff's completeness theorem this equals derivability from S plus the loop axioms; restricting M to universe Type is harmless since the relevant models are quotients of the countable term algebra. A basis is required to be a subset of laws L (standard; the implication direction alone would be the same notion since L itself satisfies S).

Nilpotency is Bruck's central nilpotency, encoded as existence of a finite central series. Normal subloops are represented by their congruences θ i (equivalence relations compatible with *, ldiv, /); a central series is a chain θ 0 = Eq ≤ θ 1 ≤ … ≤ θ n = ⊤ such that every m with θ (i+1) 1 m is central modulo θ i (commutes and lies in the left/middle/right nucleus modulo θ i), i.e. N_{i+1}/N_i ≤ Z(L/N_i). This is equivalent to the upper central series reaching L, the reading given in the decomposition notes. Requiring `∀ i, IsCongruence (θ i)` for all i (not just i ≤ n) is harmless since a series can be padded with ⊤.

Congruences are required to be compatible with ldiv and / as well as *, as is standard for the variety of loops; for finite loops multiplicative compatibility would already imply this, so no generality is lost or gained for the statement.

Boundary checks: the trivial loop is nilpotent and finitely based (proved as a test), so it is not a spurious witness; nilpotent loops that are groups are excluded by Oates–Powell; a central series of length 1 forces an abelian group, so IsNilpotent is not vacuous (abelian groups are nilpotent, proved as a test).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.4

by M. R. Vaughan-Lee

Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws.

A loop is a set with a binary operation `*`, a two-sided identity `1`, and unique left and
right division; the *loop signature* is `(*, ⧵, /, 1)`, in which loops form a variety.
The *laws* of a loop $L$ are the identities `s ≈ t` between terms of this signature that hold
under every assignment of the variables in $L$. The laws of $L$ have a *finite basis* if some
finite set of identities has exactly the laws of $L$ as its equational consequences (in the
class of all algebras of the loop signature; since loops are defined by finitely many
identities, restricting to loops gives the same notion).
"Nilpotent" is Bruck's central nilpotency: the upper central series
$1 = Z_0 \le Z_1 \le Z_2 \le \dots$, with $Z_{n+1}/Z_n = Z(L/Z_n)$, reaches $L$ after
finitely many steps. By the Oates–Powell theorem every finite group has a finite basis for
its laws; the problem asks for a finite nilpotent loop showing that the loop analogue fails.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.4»

/-- An algebra in the signature of loops: a multiplication `*`, a constant `1`, a left
division `⧵` and a right division `/`. No axioms are imposed. -/
class LoopSignature (α : Type*) extends Mul α, One α, Div α where
  /-- Left division: in a loop, `a ⧵ b` is the solution `x` of `a * x = b`. -/
  ldiv : α → α → α

@[inherit_doc] local infixl:70 " ⧵ " => LoopSignature.ldiv

/-- A loop: an algebra `(L, *, ⧵, /, 1)` in the loop signature in which `1` is a two-sided
identity, `a ⧵ b` is the unique solution `x` of `a * x = b`, and `a / b` is the unique
solution `y` of `y * b = a`. -/
class Loop (α : Type*) extends LoopSignature α where
  one_mul : ∀ a : α, 1 * a = a
  mul_one : ∀ a : α, a * 1 = a
  mul_ldiv : ∀ a b : α, a * (a ⧵ b) = b
  ldiv_mul : ∀ a b : α, a ⧵ (a * b) = b
  rdiv_mul : ∀ a b : α, (a / b) * b = a
  mul_rdiv : ∀ a b : α, (a * b) / b = a

/-- Terms in the signature of loops, with variables indexed by `ℕ`. -/
inductive LoopTerm
  | var : ℕ → LoopTerm
  | one : LoopTerm
  | mul : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | ldiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | rdiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm

/-- The value of a term in an algebra `α` of the loop signature under an assignment `v` of the
variables. -/
def LoopTerm.eval {α : Type*} [LoopSignature α] (v : ℕ → α) : LoopTerm → α
  | var n => v n
  | one => 1
  | mul s t => s.eval v * t.eval v
  | ldiv s t => s.eval v ⧵ t.eval v
  | rdiv s t => s.eval v / t.eval v

/-- A law (identity) in the loop signature is a pair of terms `(s, t)`, read as `s ≈ t`. -/
abbrev LoopLaw := LoopTerm × LoopTerm

/-- The algebra `α` satisfies the law `s ≈ t` if `s` and `t` take the same value under every
assignment of the variables in `α`. -/
def LoopSignature.Satisfies (α : Type*) [LoopSignature α] (e : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → α, e.1.eval v = e.2.eval v

/-- The laws of `α`: the set of all identities in the loop signature holding in `α`. -/
def LoopSignature.laws (α : Type*) [LoopSignature α] : Set LoopLaw :=
  {e | LoopSignature.Satisfies α e}

/-- The law `e` is an equational consequence of the set of laws `S`: every algebra of the loop
signature satisfying all laws in `S` satisfies `e`. By Birkhoff's completeness theorem this
agrees with derivability of `e` from `S` in equational logic. -/
def LoopLaw.IsConsequence (S : Set LoopLaw) (e : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ (β : Type) [LoopSignature β], (∀ e' ∈ S, LoopSignature.Satisfies β e') →
    LoopSignature.Satisfies β e

/-- The laws of `α` have a finite basis: there is a finite set `S` of laws whose equational
consequences are exactly the laws of `α`. -/
def LoopSignature.HasFiniteBasis (α : Type*) [LoopSignature α] : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set LoopLaw, S.Finite ∧ ∀ e, LoopLaw.IsConsequence S e ↔ e ∈ LoopSignature.laws α

namespace Loop

variable {L : Type*} [Loop L]

/-- `a` is congruent to `b` modulo the subset `N`, i.e. `a ∈ b * N`. When `N` is a normal
subloop this says that `a` and `b` have the same image in the quotient loop `L / N`. -/
def CongrMod (N : Set L) (a b : L) : Prop :=
  ∃ n ∈ N, a = b * n

/-- The centre of `L` modulo `N`: the elements that commute and associate (in every position)
with all elements of `L` modulo `N`. When `N` is a normal subloop this is the preimage of the
centre `Z(L / N)` of the quotient loop under the quotient map `L → L / N`. -/
def centerMod (N : Set L) : Set L :=
  {a | ∀ x y : L, CongrMod N (a * x) (x * a) ∧
    CongrMod N (a * x * y) (a * (x * y)) ∧
    CongrMod N (x * a * y) (x * (a * y)) ∧
    CongrMod N (x * y * a) (x * (y * a))}

/-- The centre of the loop `L`: the elements that commute with every element and associate
with every pair of elements in every position, i.e. the intersection of the nucleus with the
commutant. -/
def center (L : Type*) [Loop L] : Set L :=
  {a | ∀ x y : L, a * x = x * a ∧ a * x * y = a * (x * y) ∧
    x * a * y = x * (a * y) ∧ x * y * a = x * (y * a)}

/-- The upper central series of the loop `L`: `Z₀ = {1}` and `Z_{n+1} / Z_n = Z(L / Z_n)`. -/
def upperCentralSeries (L : Type*) [Loop L] : ℕ → Set L
  | 0 => {1}
  | n + 1 => centerMod (upperCentralSeries L n)

/-- A loop is centrally nilpotent (in the sense of Bruck) if its upper central series reaches
the whole loop after finitely many steps. -/
def IsCentrallyNilpotent (L : Type*) [Loop L] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, upperCentralSeries L n = Set.univ

/-- In a loop, `a ⧵ b` is the unique solution of `a * x = b`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem eq_ldiv_of_mul_eq {a b x : L} (h : a * x = b) : x = a ⧵ b := by
  rw [← h, Loop.ldiv_mul]

/-- In a loop, `a / b` is the unique solution of `y * b = a`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem eq_rdiv_of_mul_eq {a b y : L} (h : y * b = a) : y = a / b := by
  rw [← h, Loop.mul_rdiv]

/-- Congruence modulo the trivial subloop is equality. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem congrMod_singleton_one (a b : L) : CongrMod {1} a b ↔ a = b := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨n, rfl, rfl⟩
    exact Loop.mul_one b
  · rintro rfl
    exact ⟨1, rfl, (Loop.mul_one a).symm⟩

/-- The first term of the upper central series is the centre. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem upperCentralSeries_one : upperCentralSeries L 1 = center L := by
  ext a
  simp [upperCentralSeries, centerMod, center, congrMod_singleton_one]

end Loop

Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws.

That is, there is a finite loop $L$ which is centrally nilpotent (its upper central series

-/

    ∃ (L : Type) (_ : Loop L), Finite L ∧ Loop.IsCentrallyNilpotent L ∧
      ¬ LoopSignature.HasFiniteBasis L := by

/-!
# Conjecture 8.4

by M. R. Vaughan-Lee

Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«8.4»

/-- A loop, presented in its equational signature with multiplication, left and right
division, and an identity element. -/
class Loop (L : Type*) where
  one : L
  mul : L → L → L
  ldiv : L → L → L
  rdiv : L → L → L
  one_mul : ∀ x, mul one x = x
  mul_one : ∀ x, mul x one = x
  ldiv_mul : ∀ x y, ldiv x (mul x y) = y
  mul_ldiv : ∀ x y, mul x (ldiv x y) = y
  rdiv_mul : ∀ x y, rdiv (mul x y) y = x
  mul_rdiv : ∀ x y, mul (rdiv x y) y = x

/-- Terms in the loop signature, with variables indexed by natural numbers. -/
inductive LoopTerm where
  | var : ℕ → LoopTerm
  | one : LoopTerm
  | mul : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | ldiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | rdiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  deriving DecidableEq

namespace LoopTerm

/-- Evaluation of a term in a loop. -/
def eval {L : Type*} [Loop L] (v : ℕ → L) : LoopTerm → L
  | var n => v n
  | one => Loop.one
  | mul s t => Loop.mul (eval v s) (eval v t)
  | ldiv s t => Loop.ldiv (eval v s) (eval v t)
  | rdiv s t => Loop.rdiv (eval v s) (eval v t)

/-- Simultaneous substitution of loop terms for variables. -/
def subst (σ : ℕ → LoopTerm) : LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | var n => σ n
  | one => one
  | mul s t => mul (subst σ s) (subst σ t)
  | ldiv s t => ldiv (subst σ s) (subst σ t)
  | rdiv s t => rdiv (subst σ s) (subst σ t)

end LoopTerm

/-- An identity (law) in the loop signature. -/
abbrev LoopLaw := LoopTerm × LoopTerm

/-- A loop satisfies an identity if its two terms have the same value under every
assignment of the variables. -/
def Satisfies {L : Type*} [Loop L] (law : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → L, law.1.eval v = law.2.eval v

/-- Derivability from a set of identities in ordinary equational logic. -/
inductive EqConsequence (basis : Set LoopLaw) : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → Prop
  | axiom {s t} : (s, t) ∈ basis → EqConsequence basis s t
  | refl (s) : EqConsequence basis s s
  | symm {s t} : EqConsequence basis s t → EqConsequence basis t s
  | trans {s t u} : EqConsequence basis s t → EqConsequence basis t u →
      EqConsequence basis s u
  | mul {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂} : EqConsequence basis s₁ t₁ → EqConsequence basis s₂ t₂ →
      EqConsequence basis (.mul s₁ s₂) (.mul t₁ t₂)
  | ldiv {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂} : EqConsequence basis s₁ t₁ → EqConsequence basis s₂ t₂ →
      EqConsequence basis (.ldiv s₁ s₂) (.ldiv t₁ t₂)
  | rdiv {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂} : EqConsequence basis s₁ t₁ → EqConsequence basis s₂ t₂ →
      EqConsequence basis (.rdiv s₁ s₂) (.rdiv t₁ t₂)
  | subst {s t} (σ : ℕ → LoopTerm) : EqConsequence basis s t →
      EqConsequence basis (s.subst σ) (t.subst σ)

/-- The laws of a loop have a finite basis if some finite set of laws of the loop
proves every law of the loop in equational logic. -/
def HasFiniteBasisOfLaws (L : Type*) [Loop L] : Prop :=
  ∃ basis : Set LoopLaw, basis.Finite ∧
    (∀ law ∈ basis, Satisfies (L := L) law) ∧
    ∀ law, Satisfies (L := L) law → EqConsequence basis law.1 law.2

/-- A congruence of a loop in the signature consisting of multiplication, left and
right division, and the identity constant. -/
structure LoopCongruence (L : Type*) [Loop L] extends Setoid L where
  mul' : ∀ {a b c d}, r a b → r c d → r (Loop.mul a c) (Loop.mul b d)
  ldiv' : ∀ {a b c d}, r a b → r c d → r (Loop.ldiv a c) (Loop.ldiv b d)
  rdiv' : ∀ {a b c d}, r a b → r c d → r (Loop.rdiv a c) (Loop.rdiv b d)

/-- An element is central modulo a congruence if its image in the quotient commutes
with every element and lies in each of the three nuclei. -/
def IsCentralModulo {L : Type*} [Loop L] (R : LoopCongruence L) (x : L) : Prop :=
  (∀ y, R.r (Loop.mul x y) (Loop.mul y x)) ∧
  (∀ y z, R.r (Loop.mul (Loop.mul x y) z) (Loop.mul x (Loop.mul y z))) ∧
  (∀ y z, R.r (Loop.mul (Loop.mul y x) z) (Loop.mul y (Loop.mul x z))) ∧
  (∀ y z, R.r (Loop.mul (Loop.mul y z) x) (Loop.mul y (Loop.mul z x)))

/-- Bruck central nilpotency: the loop has a finite central congruence series from
equality to the universal congruence. -/
def IsCentrallyNilpotent (L : Type*) [Loop L] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ R : Fin (n + 1) → LoopCongruence L,
    (∀ x y, (R 0).r x y ↔ x = y) ∧
    (∀ x y, (R (Fin.last n)).r x y) ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n,
      (∀ x y, (R i.castSucc).r x y → (R i.succ).r x y) ∧
      ∀ x, (R i.succ).r x Loop.one → IsCentralModulo (R i.castSucc) x

/--
Construct a finite centrally nilpotent loop whose laws in the loop signature
$(1,\,\cdot,\,\backslash,\,/)$ have no finite basis.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.4» :
    ∃ (L : Type) (_ : Loop L), Finite L ∧ IsCentrallyNilpotent L ∧
      ¬ HasFiniteBasisOfLaws L := by
  sorry

by M. R. Vaughan-Lee

A loop is a set with a binary multiplication, a two-sided identity element $1$ and unique
left and right division, written $x \backslash y$ and $y / x$. Nilpotency is Bruck's central
nilpotency: the upper central series $1 = Z_0 \le Z_1 \le \dotsb$, where $Z_{n+1}/Z_n$ is the
center of $L/Z_n$, reaches $L$ after finitely many steps. The laws of a loop $L$ are the
identities $s = t$, in the signature $(\cdot, \backslash, /, 1)$, that hold in $L$. They have
a finite basis if some finite set of laws of $L$ implies all laws of $L$, i.e. every loop
satisfying the finitely many chosen laws satisfies every law of $L$. Since the loop axioms are
themselves laws of $L$, it makes no difference whether consequences are taken among all loops or
among all algebras of this signature. For finite groups a finite basis always exists (the
Oates–Powell theorem).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

/-- A loop: a type with a multiplication `*`, a two-sided identity `1`, a left division `ldiv`
(written `x ⧵ y`, the unique solution `z` of `x * z = y`) and a right division `/`
(`y / x` is the unique solution `z` of `z * x = y`). -/

  /-- Left division: `ldiv x y` is the unique `z` with `x * z = y`. -/

  one_mul : ∀ x : L, 1 * x = x
  mul_one : ∀ x : L, x * 1 = x
  mul_ldiv : ∀ x y : L, x * ldiv x y = y
  ldiv_mul : ∀ x y : L, ldiv x (x * y) = y
  div_mul : ∀ x y : L, y / x * x = y
  mul_div : ∀ x y : L, y * x / x = y

/-- Terms in the signature `(*, ⧵, /, 1)` of loops, over the variables `ℕ`. -/
inductive LoopTerm
  | var : ℕ → LoopTerm
  | one : LoopTerm
  | mul : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | ldiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | div : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm

variable {L : Type*} [Loop L]

/-- The value of a term in a loop `L` under an assignment `v` of the variables. -/
def LoopTerm.eval (v : ℕ → L) : LoopTerm → L
  | var n => v n
  | one => 1
  | mul s t => s.eval v * t.eval v
  | ldiv s t => s.eval v ⧵ t.eval v
  | div s t => s.eval v / t.eval v

/-- A loop `L` satisfies the law `s = t` (given as the pair `(s, t)`) if `s` and `t` take the
same value in `L` under every assignment of the variables. -/
def Satisfies (L : Type*) [Loop L] (e : LoopTerm × LoopTerm) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → L, e.1.eval v = e.2.eval v

def laws (L : Type*) [Loop L] : Set (LoopTerm × LoopTerm) :=
  {e | Satisfies L e}

/-- The laws of a loop `L` have a finite basis if there is a finite set `S` of laws of `L` such
that every law of `L` is a consequence of `S`, i.e. every loop satisfying all laws in `S`
satisfies all laws of `L`. -/

  ∃ S : Set (LoopTerm × LoopTerm), S.Finite ∧ S ⊆ laws L ∧
    ∀ (M : Type) [Loop M], (∀ e ∈ S, Satisfies M e) → ∀ e ∈ laws L, Satisfies M e

/-- An element `a` is central modulo a subset `N` of `L` if it commutes and associates with all
elements of `L` up to `N`: `a * x ∈ (x * a) * N`, `(a * x) * y ∈ (a * (x * y)) * N`,

for `N = {1}` it says that `a` lies in the center of `L`. -/
def IsCentralMod (N : Set L) (a : L) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : L, (x * a) ⧵ (a * x) ∈ N ∧ (a * (x * y)) ⧵ (a * x * y) ∈ N ∧
    (x * (a * y)) ⧵ (x * a * y) ∈ N ∧ (x * (y * a)) ⧵ (x * y * a) ∈ N

  | 0 => {1}
  | n + 1 => {a | IsCentralMod (upperCentralSeries L n) a}

finitely many steps. -/

  ∃ n, upperCentralSeries L n = Set.univ

    rwa [Loop.mul_one] at this

    a ∈ upperCentralSeries L 1 ↔ ∀ x y : L, a * x = x * a ∧ a * x * y = a * (x * y) ∧

  simp [upperCentralSeries, IsCentralMod, ldiv_eq_one_iff]

namespace Kourovka.«8.4»

/-- A loop, with left and right division included as primitive operations. -/
structure Loop where
  Carrier : Type
  one : Carrier
  mul : Carrier → Carrier → Carrier
  ldiv : Carrier → Carrier → Carrier
  rdiv : Carrier → Carrier → Carrier
  one_mul : ∀ x, mul one x = x
  mul_one : ∀ x, mul x one = x
  ldiv_mul : ∀ x y, ldiv x (mul x y) = y
  mul_ldiv : ∀ x y, mul x (ldiv x y) = y
  mul_rdiv : ∀ x y, rdiv (mul x y) y = x
  rdiv_mul : ∀ x y, mul (rdiv x y) y = x

/-- Terms in the loop signature, with variables indexed by natural numbers. -/
inductive LoopTerm where
  | var : ℕ → LoopTerm
  | one : LoopTerm
  | mul : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | ldiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | rdiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- Evaluation of a term in a loop under an assignment of its variables. -/
def LoopTerm.eval (L : Loop) (v : ℕ → L.Carrier) : LoopTerm → L.Carrier
  | .var n => v n
  | .one => L.one
  | .mul s t => L.mul (s.eval L v) (t.eval L v)
  | .ldiv s t => L.ldiv (s.eval L v) (t.eval L v)
  | .rdiv s t => L.rdiv (s.eval L v) (t.eval L v)

/-- An identity (law) in the signature of loops. -/
abbrev LoopLaw := LoopTerm × LoopTerm

/-- A loop satisfies a law when the two terms agree under every assignment. -/
def Satisfies (L : Loop) (e : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → L.Carrier, e.1.eval L v = e.2.eval L v

/-- Semantic equational consequence within the variety of loops. -/
def Entails (E : Set LoopLaw) (e : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ L : Loop, (∀ f ∈ E, Satisfies L f) → Satisfies L e

/-- The laws of a loop are finitely based if some finite collection of its laws entails every law
of the loop. -/
def IsFinitelyBased (L : Loop) : Prop :=
  ∃ E : Finset LoopLaw,
    (∀ e ∈ E, Satisfies L e) ∧ ∀ e, Satisfies L e → Entails (E : Set LoopLaw) e

/-- A subloop, recorded as a subset closed under all operations in the loop signature. -/
structure Subloop (L : Loop) where
  carrier : Set L.Carrier
  one_mem : L.one ∈ carrier
  mul_mem : ∀ {x y}, x ∈ carrier → y ∈ carrier → L.mul x y ∈ carrier
  ldiv_mem : ∀ {x y}, x ∈ carrier → y ∈ carrier → L.ldiv x y ∈ carrier
  rdiv_mem : ∀ {x y}, x ∈ carrier → y ∈ carrier → L.rdiv x y ∈ carrier

/-- A normal subloop, represented by a compatible loop congruence whose identity class is the
subloop. -/
structure NormalSubloop (L : Loop) extends Subloop L where
  congruence : Setoid L.Carrier
  mul_compatible : ∀ {a b c d}, congruence.r a b → congruence.r c d →
    congruence.r (L.mul a c) (L.mul b d)
  ldiv_compatible : ∀ {a b c d}, congruence.r a b → congruence.r c d →
    congruence.r (L.ldiv a c) (L.ldiv b d)
  rdiv_compatible : ∀ {a b c d}, congruence.r a b → congruence.r c d →
    congruence.r (L.rdiv a c) (L.rdiv b d)
  rel_one_iff : ∀ x, congruence.r x L.one ↔ x ∈ carrier

/-- Membership of a normal subloop. -/
def NormalSubloop.Mem {L : Loop} (N : NormalSubloop L) (x : L.Carrier) : Prop :=
  x ∈ N.carrier

/-- A finite central series for a loop. At each step, the next normal subloop modulo the preceding
one lies in the center of the corresponding quotient loop. -/
def HasCentralSeries (L : Loop) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ N : Fin (n + 1) → NormalSubloop L,
    (∀ x, (N 0).Mem x ↔ x = L.one) ∧
    (∀ x, (N (Fin.last n)).Mem x) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin n, ∀ x, (N i.castSucc).Mem x → (N i.succ).Mem x) ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, ∀ a, (N i.succ).Mem a → ∀ x y,
      let R := (N i.castSucc).congruence.r
      R (L.mul a x) (L.mul x a) ∧
      R (L.mul (L.mul a x) y) (L.mul a (L.mul x y)) ∧
      R (L.mul (L.mul x a) y) (L.mul x (L.mul a y)) ∧
      R (L.mul (L.mul x y) a) (L.mul x (L.mul y a))

/-- A loop is centrally nilpotent when it has a finite central series. -/
def IsCentrallyNilpotent (L : Loop) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, HasCentralSeries L n

nilpotence in the sense of Bruck, and laws and their consequences are taken in the full loop
signature consisting of the identity, multiplication, left division, and right division.

def LawHolds {L : Type} (loop : Loop L) (law : LoopLaw) : Prop :=

def laws {L : Type} (loop : Loop L) : Set LoopLaw :=
  {law | LawHolds loop law}

def Entails (S : Set LoopLaw) (law : LoopLaw) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : Type) (loop : Loop M), (∀ e ∈ S, LawHolds loop e) → LawHolds loop law

/-- A finite basis for the laws of a loop is a finite subset of its laws from
which every law of the loop is an equational consequence. -/
def HasFiniteBasis {L : Type} (loop : Loop L) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : Set LoopLaw, B.Finite ∧ B ⊆ laws loop ∧
    ∀ law ∈ laws loop, Entails B law

division operations. -/
structure LoopCongruence {L : Type} (loop : Loop L) where
  rel : L → L → Prop
  refl : ∀ x, rel x x
  symm : ∀ {x y}, rel x y → rel y x
  trans : ∀ {x y z}, rel x y → rel y z → rel x z

Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws. Here
nilpotence is Bruck central nilpotence, and laws and their consequences are
interpreted in the full loop signature consisting of the identity,
multiplication, left division, and right division.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]

    ∃ (L : Type) (loop : Loop L),
      Finite L ∧ IsCentrallyNilpotent loop ∧ ¬ HasFiniteBasis loop := by
